# 02 A flowchart stops swallowing the shapes it does not draw

## Outcome

`A[(DB)]`, `A[[Sub]]`, `A[/Para/]`, `A[\Alt\]` and a Markdown string are rejected with a
diagnostic naming what they are, instead of being drawn as rectangles labelled `(DB)`, `[Sub]`,
`/Para/`, `\Alt\`.

## Why this ticket exists

`NODE_RE` is `/^(\w+)\s*\[([^\]]*)\]\s*(?::::(\w+))?\s*$/`. The `[^\]]*` swallows whatever is
inside the brackets and calls it a label, so **every bracket shape Mermaid has and Siren does not
draw becomes a mislabelled rectangle with no diagnostic**. Measured: five of the 39 flowchart
cases fail this way.

That was a defensible choice under "we support a subset of Mermaid" — a lenient parser rendered
more documents. Under "a document that renders in Mermaid must render here" it is the worst
option available, because it disguises *not implemented* as *supported* and hides the gap from
the very instrument built to measure it.

Rejecting is not the end state. The shapes get implemented on their own board. This ticket makes
the interim state honest.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `A[(DB)]`, `A[[Sub]]`, `A[/Para/]`, `A[\Alt\]` and `A[/Trap\]` each produce an
      error-severity diagnostic. The message names the shape Mermaid means — an author who wrote a
      cylinder should be told Siren does not draw a cylinder yet, not that their line is
      unrecognized.
- [x] A Markdown string label (`A["`+"`"+`**bold**`+"`"+`"]`) is likewise rejected rather than
      drawn with its backticks and asterisks intact.
- [x] **`A[plain label]` still works, and so does every label an existing test or example uses.**
      This ticket narrows what is accepted; a label that is not trying to be another shape must be
      untouched. Grep `examples/` before you finish — no example may break.
- [x] A label containing a bracket-ish character that is *not* a shape opener keeps working:
      `A[a/b]`, `A[x (y)]`, `A[100%]`. Assert these, because the obvious over-tight regex breaks
      them and an over-tight parser is its own compatibility bug.
- [x] The corpus's five `silently-wrong` **flowchart** entries become `rejected`, their `assert`s
      updated, and **both ratchet numbers updated**. The literals as you inherit them are
      `SILENTLY_WRONG = 8` and `REJECTED = 33`; after this ticket they should be **3 and 38**.
      Your report states both, because "the numbers got worse" is the expected result here and a
      reader needs to see you meant it.
- [x] **Do not touch the two sequence entries in `silently-wrong`.** `seq-loop` and `seq-alt-else`
      are there because Siren never draws a control-flow block's keyword — the ratchet's own
      comment names them and explains that their exit is implementation, not rejection. They are a
      later board's. The 3 you leave behind is 2 of those plus one sequence activation case, which
      ticket 03 takes.
- [x] A comment at the regex says why it refuses rather than swallows, and points at the board's
      policy. The next person to widen this pattern needs the reason in front of them.

## Status

Done (2026-09-06), commit 2937fa7. 8 slices (7 red-green, 1 declared characterization).
685 core tests / 29 board, tsc clean both. Ratchets: silently-wrong 8 → 3, rejected 33 → 38.

Extended beyond the ticket to refuse shapes at an EDGE ENDPOINT too — `EDGE_RE` carries the
same `[^\]]*`, so the policy would otherwise have held in only one of the two places a label
can be written.

The write scope omitted `corpus.test.ts` while the packet ordered the edit it holds. The
planner's error; the worker made the edit and flagged it.
